title: A. A Name of One's Own

legend: A new social network is launching, where n%%ZSMJ0%% people sign up one by one. The i%%ZSMJ1%%-th person has two usernames in mind, xi%%ZSMJ2%% and yi%%ZSMJ3%% (xi≠yi%%ZSMJ4%%), and must register under exactly one of them. No two people may share a username.

For each k%%ZSMJ5%% from 1%%ZSMJ6%% to n%%ZSMJ7%%, please count, modulo 998244353%%ZSMJ8%%, the number of ways to give each of the first k%%ZSMJ9%% people one of their two chosen usernames so that all k%%ZSMJ10%% chosen usernames are distinct.
input: The first line contains a single integer t%%ZSMJ11%% (1≤t≤104%%ZSMJ12%%) — the number of test cases.
The first line of each test case contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ13%% (1≤n≤3⋅105%%ZSMJ14%%) — the number of people.
The i%%ZSMJ15%%-th of the next n%%ZSMJ16%% lines contains two integers xi%%ZSMJ17%% and yi%%ZSMJ18%% (1≤xi,yi≤109%%ZSMJ19%%, xi≠yi%%ZSMJ20%%) — the two usernames person i%%ZSMJ21%% has in mind.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ22%% over all test cases does not exceed 3⋅105%%ZSMJ23%%.
output: For each test case, print n%%ZSMJ24%% space-separated integers; the k%%ZSMJ25%%-th of them is the number of valid username assignments for the first k%%ZSMJ26%% people, taken modulo 998244353%%ZSMJ27%%.
note: In the first test case, the single person may sign up as 1%%ZSMJ28%% or 2%%ZSMJ29%%, so there are 2%%ZSMJ30%% ways.

In the fourth test case, with only the first person there are 2%%ZSMJ31%% ways. With the first two people, every combination works except both taking 2%%ZSMJ32%%, so there are 3%%ZSMJ33%% ways. With all three people, out of the 8%%ZSMJ34%% combinations only (1,2,3)%%ZSMJ35%% and (2,3,1)%%ZSMJ36%% leave no two people sharing a username, so there are 2%%ZSMJ37%% ways.
